# Argos VSP — Q2 2026 Quarterly Summary

**Period:** April 1 – June 15, 2026 · **Lead Engineer:** Yoad Oxman
**Full version:** [Q2-2026-summary.docx](Q2-2026-summary.docx) (generated by [generate_q2_summary.py](../_research-tools/generators/generate_q2_summary.py)) · **Prior snapshot:** [project-summary.docx](project-summary.docx) (Q1, March 11, 2026)

## At a glance

In Q2 2026, Argos went from a research prototype to a product running on clients' machines, with
real outside interest building. The most important advance was confidence scoring — it's what makes
the system actually usable: it tells operators which whole videos to trust and which to set aside, and
within each usable video which words are reliable and which aren't. Without it the raw output isn't
dependable enough to act on. We also changed how the model answers — instead of its single best guess,
it now weighs many alternative readings of each clip and returns the consensus, making the output
useful noticeably more often (now roughly six in ten clips) — estimated that the system on its own is
about as good as a skilled deaf lip-reader and clearly beats both when paired with a human reviewer,
and prepared an upgrade to a stronger underlying language model. On delivery, we built a standalone
version for both Ubuntu and the clients' Windows machines (including fully offline/air-gapped), worked
through the deployment issues that surfaced, and ran a major stakeholder meeting that sharpened what
clients actually need and drew a lot of "this is useful" — with strong interest now from three
separate groups, one of which handed us 100 hours of real footage to evaluate. Next quarter focuses on
the model upgrade, evaluating that 100-hour client footage, a human-comparison study, and the clients'
top requests: handling multiple speakers and Arabic.
